title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
title_zh: 人工智能辅助的临床表型分型：人类棕色脂肪
abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans. Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.
abstract_zh: 脂肪组织在体能平衡中起核心作用，与肥胖及其并发症的病理生理过程密切相关1,2。与白色脂肪组织不同，棕色脂肪组织（BAT）利用能量产生热量3。人类中可检测到的BAT与心代谢疾病患病率降低有关4。然而，与BAT相关的健康状况完整光谱仍不清楚，且缺乏人类BAT活量的高通量方法5,6。本研究利用大数据和人工智能，在一家大型癌症中心101,243名患者的队列中系统定义BAT的临床影响。我们的无偏分析表明，在所有诊断中，心血管疾病和精神疾病在有BAT的人群中患病率较低。利用机器学习方法，我们半自动化地量化了约8,700名患者的BAT活性，并证明BAT活性较高，特别是在腋下脂肪垫，与心代谢疾病的较低几率以及更健康的白色脂肪分布相关。有BAT的人群还表现出更有利的血糖参数、脂质谱、炎症标记物和超声心动图指标。药物使用分析显示，血管紧张素受体阻滞剂的使用与BAT的存在呈正相关。作为概念验证，我们证明血管紧张素受体阻滞剂洛沙坦可增加棕色脂肪细胞活性和全身能量消耗。总之，我们利用人工智能和大数据识别出与BAT相关的新临床表型，并作为人体激活该组织的药物再利用平台。人工智能辅助的BAT活性量化和分析揭示了BAT与更有利的代谢概况以及较低的精神疾病率之间的联系，并可识别可重新利用以激活人体该组织的药物化学代理。
